subject: Garden Guru input/composer surface (viewer.html ~4199-4251): textarea + labeled-emoji icon row (Voice/Photo) + twin commit buttons (Save to journal / Ask Garden Guru). Scoped to making the composer feel familiar/native by borrowing established AI-chat + iPhone-native composer conventions, WITHOUT collapsing the protected two-intent Save/Ask split.
review_level: screen-component (the composer only; not the whole Guru flow)

user_context.primary_user: Mom (make-or-break daily user, device d-14nyhnjz, 27/~40 active days). Paul-mobile is the secondary performer (on-property, voice-friendly, weak signal).
core_jobs_to_be_done: Ask the property a plain-language question and feel confident it was heard (Mom's mental model = ASK, not log).
Log something noticed, deterministically, and be sure it was kept ('I hoped it was logged but wasn't sure').
Do both from a one-handed, reclined, half-engaged glance in ~1.5s, at no-glasses text size, on possibly-weak rural signal.
user_context.context_of_use: iPhone 393x793. Mom: bed/coffee or evening wind-down, one hand, half-attended, A/A+ large-type user, ChatGPT-anxiety. Paul-mobile: on the property, one hand occupied, voice-primary, outdoor legibility, Bortle-3 weak connectivity.
assumptions_made: The composer's job, position (beneath the latest reply per Phase 1), warm-tan field-journal skin, and the protected symmetric two-intent commit are all settled inputs from the fact base — not relitigated here.
This review redesigns the composer's control grammar (icon row, mic, glyphs, commit affordance shape), not the conversation flow, the fences, or the persistence model.
The exact 'photo shows a different picture' bug (F4 in the fact base) is unreproduced; treated here as most-likely the decorative-emoji-render issue, pending Paul's device description.
user_context.user_context_confidence: medium-high — personas + JTBDs are validated in prior research; this specific composer control redesign is inferred from those, not yet Mom-tested.

conventionsSurvey.note: Durable conventions extracted from current (2026) iPhone-native and AI-chat composers. Web-search-confirmed the current landscape (iOS 26 Messages, ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini iOS 2026); the composer grammar itself has been stable for years and is described from established design conventions, not invented.

durable_patterns: FIELD IS THE HERO. One rounded text field dominates; controls are subordinate to it, tucked at its edges or in a thin toolbar above the keyboard. There is no row of labeled utility buttons under the field.

ATTACH LIVES LEFT / OUTSIDE. iMessage consolidated its attachment affordances into a single '+' to the LEFT of the field (camera/photos/apps behind it). Notes/Mail put camera+attachment in a quiet toolbar above the keyboard. Attachment is one small monochrome glyph, never a big colored labeled button.

SEND LIVES RIGHT / INLINE, AND ACTIVATES ON CONTENT. A single glyph (up-arrow, circled arrow) sits at the field's right edge; it is dimmed/absent when the field is empty and colors/appears once there's text. Emptiness disables it — the state IS the affordance.

DICTATION IS A KEYBOARD AFFORDANCE, NOT AN APP CONTROL. The mic key next to the spacebar is the native dictation entry point on every text field. Users already have it 'for free'; apps rarely reimplement it. (iOS 26 improved dictation further — spell-out-names, studio-quality capture.)
GLYPHS ARE MONOCHROME SF-SYMBOL-STYLE, UNLABELED. No emoji, no text labels on inline controls. The register is quiet-utility, not toolbar.
ONE ROUNDED COMPOSER, field-as-hero, same as native.
ATTACHMENT = LEFT '+' / PAPERCLIP (photos, camera, files behind one glyph). ChatGPT consolidated to a single '+'; iOS photo capture/upload was made 'faster and smoother' in 2026.

RIGHT EDGE HOLDS VOICE **AND** SEND, STATE-SWITCHED. Empty field: the right side shows voice affordances (a dictation waveform + a separate full 'voice mode' button). Once text is typed, a send arrow appears/replaces. Send turns into a STOP square during generation.
TWO DISTINCT VOICE THINGS. (a) dictation = speech-to-text into the field (mic glyph); (b) voice mode = a live spoken conversation (waveform/headphone glyph). They are not the same control.
'THINKING' IS SHOWN IN-THREAD WHERE THE ANSWER WILL APPEAR — a shimmer / pulsing dots / streaming text at the reply location, plus the send-to-stop swap. The button alone is not the only signal.
MONOCHROME GLYPHS, NO EMOJI, NO LABELS on the composer controls.

cross_world_durables: One field is the hero; controls are subordinate and live at its edges.
Attachment = left; commit/send = right. This spatial mapping is rock-solid across both worlds.
The commit control activates on content and is dimmed/absent when empty — state carries the affordance.

Inline controls are monochrome, unlabeled, ignorable — NOT a labeled utility toolbar. (The current build's labeled '🎤 Voice / 📷 Photo' row is precisely the toolbar register both worlds have moved away from.)
Dictation is a mic glyph users already recognize — and on native iOS it's a more reliable keyboard affordance the app doesn't need to rebuild.
Progress/thinking renders in-thread at the answer's location, not only on the button.
conventionsSurvey.the_one_convention_fernwood_must_decline: Both worlds converge on a SINGLE send/commit control. Fernwood's protected two-intent split (Save=no-AI vs Ask=AI, symmetric, never auto-routed) cannot adopt single-send without breaking the capture principle. So the play is: borrow the native FIELD grammar wholesale, and decline single-send at the COMMIT — substituting a two-action button row, which is itself a native iOS idiom (Mail's send row, two-button alert dialogs, share-sheet actions), so familiarity survives the one departure.

layoutOptions.name: Native field + twin commit row (RECOMMENDED)
layoutOptions.wireframe:
+-------------------------------------------+
|  What did you see, or want to know?        |   <- hero field, warm-tan, no hard border at rest
|                                            |
|  [camera]                        [mic]     |   <- monochrome line glyphs at the field's edges: attach LEFT, mic RIGHT (both inline, unlabeled, quiet)
+-------------------------------------------+
+---------------------+ +-------------------+
|   Save to journal   | |   Ask the Guru    |   <- two co-equal WORD-LED commit buttons, symmetric weight
+---------------------+ +-------------------+
layoutOptions.borrows: iMessage/Notes field-as-hero; attach-left + control-right inline glyph placement; monochrome SF-Symbol-style glyphs replacing labeled emoji; mic inside the field's right edge (the exact iOS-native pattern, also the unfulfilled unified-input F8 spec).
layoutOptions.keeps_save_ask_legible: The two intents stay as two co-equal, word-led buttons below the field — symmetric weight (cross-project candidate), routing carried by TEXT+size+position (Mom no-glasses constraint), never color, never a hidden mode, never auto-routed. The twin-button commit row reads as native because two-action rows are a familiar iOS idiom.
layoutOptions.tradeoffs: Slightly taller than a pure single-send composer (the commit row costs one row of height). Declines the single-send convention on purpose — but substitutes a natively-familiar two-action row, so it doesn't read as invented UI.
layoutOptions.reads_for_mom: The field looks like Notes/iMessage — familiar, unthreatening, not a chatbot. Two large legible buttons she can read at no-glasses size; the choice is WORDS, not icons or color. Camera + mic are small, optional, ignorable — they don't compete for the glance. Passes the 1.5s half-engagement read.

layoutOptions.name: Intent-tab + single send (native segmented control)
layoutOptions.wireframe:
+-- Note --+-- Ask ---+                          <- iOS segmented control declares intent BEFORE sending
+-------------------------------------------+
|  What did you see?         [camera] [mic] |   <- single field, attach + mic inline
|                                       [>] |   <- ONE send glyph, right edge, activates on text
+-------------------------------------------+
layoutOptions.borrows: The single-composer convention harder (true single send-arrow, right edge, activates on content); iOS segmented control (a native primitive) to declare Save-vs-Ask.
layoutOptions.keeps_save_ask_legible: The split moves UP-FRONT: the tab you're on declares the intent before you send. Send stays one glyph.
layoutOptions.tradeoffs: Introduces MODE. The input's meaning now depends on which tab is active — a hidden-state risk (Nielsen #1 visibility of system status). This is exactly the 'which tab is active / auto-detection fragility' the Houseplants candidate 'Scope is communicated by where you tap' warns against. For Mom at half-engagement: she types a note with the tab silently on 'Ask', accidentally spends an AI call / gets a chatbot reply she didn't want. A mode she must notice-and-set before typing is arguably WORSE than the two-button choice-at-commit, and it edges toward routing-by-mode rather than routing-by-explicit-tap. NOT recommended.
layoutOptions.reads_for_mom: Risk of silent wrong-mode. The segmented control is small and sits away from her focus (the field); she may never register which side is lit. Fails the half-engagement bar precisely because the consequential state is the quietest element.

layoutOptions.name: Twin send-glyphs at the right edge (max-native, wrong for Mom)
layoutOptions.wireframe:
+-------------------------------------------+
|  What did you see, or want to know?        |
|                                            |
|  [camera]                    [book] [leaf] |   <- TWO commit glyphs at the right edge; both = 'send', differ by destination
+-------------------------------------------+
layoutOptions.borrows: Maximally native: inline-send-on-the-right, most compact, no separate button row.
layoutOptions.keeps_save_ask_legible: It does NOT, for this user. The entire Save/Ask distinction now rides on two small unlabeled glyphs.
layoutOptions.tradeoffs: Fails Mom's no-glasses constraint hard: memory 'Mom reads with difficulty' requires routing carried by icon+size+color+position AND ideally text; two tiny unlabeled glyphs as the sole commit affordance is the exact 'routing-by-icon-alone' accessibility failure. Also collapses the symmetric WORD-LED button model the fact base protects. Presented only as the 'most native but wrong here' pole.
layoutOptions.reads_for_mom: Two indistinguishable specks. She can't tell Save from Ask without leaning in — the failure mode the whole large-type program exists to prevent.

principles_applied: Make every surface read at half-engagement (fernwood.md)
Glyphs follow the journal voice, not the dashboard voice (fernwood.md)
Icons earn their place — true AND useful (cross-project.md)
Explicit user-routing requires symmetric affordance weight (cross-project.md candidate)
Scope is communicated by where you tap, not auto-detected (cross-project.md candidate)
Mom reads with difficulty — routing carried by icon+size+color+position, not label text alone (memory: project_fernwood_mom_reading_accessibility)
No AI on capture; CHARACTERIZE (transcription) is an acceptable flagged middle layer (memory: feedback_no_ai_on_capture)

findings.observation: The current icon row is two LABELED EMOJI buttons ('🎤 Voice', '📷 Photo') sitting under the field as a utility toolbar. This is the exact register both native iOS and AI-chat composers have moved AWAY from — both worlds tuck attachment/mic as small monochrome unlabeled glyphs at the field's edges, not as a labeled button row beneath it. The labeled-emoji-row is also what makes the surface read as a mini productivity app rather than a journal composer.
findings.user_impact: The labeled toolbar adds visual weight and a 'this is a tool with functions' register that undercuts the field-journal feel and the discreet-by-default intent. The emoji also render inconsistently across iOS versions (the likely root of Paul's 'different picture' report). For Mom, it's more chrome to parse at half-engagement.
findings.principle_invoked: field-as-hero / attach-left inline (conventions survey); Ornament earns its place + Icons earn their place (cross-project); Glyphs follow the journal voice (fernwood).
findings.recommendation: Adopt Layout A. Dissolve the labeled icon row: move CAMERA to a single monochrome line-glyph at the field's LEFT edge, MIC (if kept — see F2) to a monochrome glyph at the field's RIGHT edge. Drop the word-labels on both (native inline controls are unlabeled). The two commit buttons below the field become the only labeled, word-led controls — which is correct, because they carry the load-bearing routing.

findings.observation: Voice rides browser webkitSpeechRecognition with a continuous-restart hack (createVoiceCapture ~12790). It's unreliable on iOS Safari and streams audio to Apple's servers — fragile on the property's weak rural signal. Meanwhile, the single most native fact: on iOS, dictation is already a KEYBOARD affordance (the mic key by the spacebar) that Mom has on every text field, backed by the OS's own (2026-improved) dictation. The app's custom 🎤 Voice button is a strictly-worse reimplementation of something the platform already gives her more reliably. And per the fact base, Mom likely won't talk to her phone in bed anyway; voice-primary is Paul-mobile's mode.
findings.user_impact: Keeping a prominent, fragile app-mic sets Mom up for a broken-feeling experience she didn't need (the keyboard mic would have worked), and it's the probable source of Paul's 'transcription problems.' It also fails Icons-earn-their-place test 2 on iOS (it duplicates a better native control).
findings.principle_invoked: Dictation-is-a-keyboard-affordance (conventions survey); Icons earn their place — true AND useful (cross-project); Defer affordances pending signal (memory). Note: transcription itself is the acceptable 'characterize' layer on the capture path (memory feedback_no_ai_on_capture), so voice-into-Save is fine in principle — the issue is the PRIMITIVE, not the intent.
findings.recommendation: De-emphasize, keep-graceful. (a) Remove the labeled 🎤 Voice button. (b) Let Mom's native keyboard mic carry her rare voice need — it's more reliable and she already knows it. (c) If a mic is kept for Paul-mobile, render it as a small monochrome glyph inside the field's right edge (native pattern), and make failure honest in journal voice ('The signal's slow up here — you can type it instead'), never a raw error string. (d) Do NOT build record→upload→server-transcribe now — it's out of scope and defer-pending-signal applies. Flag it as the RIGHT future architecture IF voice proves used (it removes cloud-streaming-during-capture and reuses the already-built Phase-H audio_ref blob pattern). Instrument: if mic use <5% at 90 days, cut the app-mic entirely and rely on the keyboard mic.

findings.observation: The two commit buttons currently lead with decorative emoji (📓 Save to journal, 🌿 Ask Garden Guru). '📓' is redundant with the word 'journal' (fails Icons-earn-their-place test 2). '🌿' is closer to an IDENTITY glyph for the Guru (the same exemption that lets the plant care-type icon lexicon stay per the fernwood glyph rule).
findings.user_impact: Minor register-leak; the book emoji is pure tax. But the commit buttons are also where Mom's routing MUST stay word-led and large — so this is a 'refine, don't strip' case, not a 'go glyph-only' case.
findings.principle_invoked: Icons earn their place (cross-project); Glyphs follow the journal voice (fernwood); Mom-reads-with-difficulty (memory).
findings.recommendation: Keep both commit buttons WORD-LED at no-glasses size (the words carry the routing). Drop the '📓' (the word 'journal' is the icon). Optionally keep a single quiet monochrome leaf/sprout as the Guru's identity mark — but as a line-glyph, not a color emoji, to hold the journal register. Never reduce these two to glyph-only (that's Layout C's failure).

findings.observation: Both surveyed worlds signal 'thinking' IN-THREAD at the answer's location (shimmer/dots/streaming) and swap send→stop during generation. The prior unified-input review (F9) already specced an in-voice pending line ('Listening…'). This is convention-aligned and worth honoring when the Ask path fires from the new composer, given weak-signal latency.
findings.user_impact: On weak rural signal, an Ask with no visible pending state invites a double-tap (duplicate query) or abandonment. The native convention (in-thread shimmer + button state change) is what users now expect.
findings.principle_invoked: 'Thinking' renders in-thread (conventions survey); Nielsen 1; Caution-as-noticing (fernwood — no red/spinner-to-error, journal-voice failure).
findings.recommendation: When Ask fires: the Ask button shifts to a soft warm pulse / 'Asking…' state, and the reply location shows an in-voice thinking line (existing 'Listening…' spec). Keep it in journal voice, never a raw spinner or error. This is confirmation/polish, not a blocker — flagged so the composer redesign carries the pending-state forward rather than dropping it.

specific_calls.voice_affordance: De-emphasize as an app control; lean on the native iOS keyboard mic (more reliable, already Mom's). If kept for Paul-mobile, an inline right-edge monochrome mic glyph with honest journal-voice failure. Do NOT build record→upload→server-transcribe now (out of scope + defer-pending-signal), but note it as the correct future architecture if voice proves used (reuses the Phase-H audio_ref blob pattern, removes cloud-streaming-during-capture). Instrument <5%-at-90-days → cut the app-mic.
specific_calls.emoji_to_glyphs: Replace the labeled 🎤/📷 icon row with monochrome SF-Symbol-style LINE glyphs tucked at the field's edges (camera left, mic right), unlabeled. Counter-intuitively this REDUCES the productivity-app feel: that feel comes from loud, colored, LABELED utility buttons in a row (what's there now); native composers are quiet monochrome edge-glyphs. For the two COMMIT buttons, keep WORDS leading (Mom's no-glasses routing); drop the redundant 📓; at most a single quiet identity line-glyph on the Guru button.
specific_calls.two_button_vs_single_composer: Yes — borrow the single-composer familiarity for the FIELD (hero field, inline attach-left, inline mic-right, monochrome glyphs, warm-tan skin) and decline single-send only at the COMMIT, substituting a two-action word-led button row (itself a native iOS idiom). This preserves the protected Save/Ask split as two co-equal WORD-LED buttons — symmetric weight, routing by text+position not color or hidden mode, never auto-routed. Reject single-send (Layout C collapses the split into unreadable glyphs) and reject the intent-tab/mode (Layout B hides consequential state from a half-engaged Mom).

open_questions_for_user: The 'photo shows a different picture' bug (fact base F4) is still unreproduced. Best guess is the decorative-emoji render — which Layout A fixes by switching to monochrome glyphs. If it's actually the iOS library-vs-camera picker or a wrong preview thumbnail, that's a separate functional bug; a one-line description or a device screenshot would settle it.

Confirm the app-mic should be kept at all for Paul-mobile, vs. fully delegating dictation to the native keyboard mic for everyone in v1 (lightest, most reliable). My lean: delegate to keyboard mic for v1, instrument, and only revive an app-mic if signal shows real use.
follow_up_research_suggested: Mom-direct: show her the Layout-A composer (field + camera/mic edge glyphs + two word-led buttons) and confirm the Save/Ask choice reads at a glance without leaning in. Lowest-cost validation of F1/F3.
Instrument app-mic invocation rate (already on record from the prior review) — the <5%-at-90-days trigger decides whether the app-mic survives at all.

principles_to_propose.principle: Borrow the native composer's field grammar; decline only the single-send convention where a protected intent-split lives
principles_to_propose.rationale: This composer surfaces a reusable move: when a familiar single-composer pattern (native or chat) conflicts with a project-protected two-intent commit, borrow the FIELD wholesale (hero field, inline edge-glyphs, monochrome controls, project skin) and substitute a two-action word-led button row for the single send — because a two-action row is itself a native idiom, so familiarity survives the one deliberate departure. Candidate; hold at one occurrence. May generalize to Houseplants' per-plant vs cross-collection ask, so worth watching for a second occurrence before proposing promotion to cross-project.

principles_to_propose.principle: Prefer the platform's native control over an app reimplementation of the same affordance — especially on the capture path
principles_to_propose.rationale: The app-mic (webkitSpeechRecognition) is a fragile reimplementation of the iOS keyboard mic Mom already has more reliably. Sharpens 'Icons earn their place — true AND useful' with a platform-delegation test: if the OS gives the user a more reliable version of this control on every field, the app's custom version usually fails test 2. Candidate; surfaced once here — watch for a second occurrence (e.g., a custom share/download control that duplicates the native share sheet) before promoting.
